PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 79 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 11/15/27 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent lower extremity edema, and ongoing mental health support.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit approximately one month after his last appointment. He reports that his respiratory symptoms have shown minimal improvement; however, he continues to experience significant dyspnea, particularly during exertion. He states that he is using his albuterol inhaler approximately six to seven times daily, particularly during physical activities and at night, where he notes increased nocturnal wheezing that disrupts his sleep.
Concerning his bilateral lower extremity edema, Mr. Fairfax describes a persistent 3+ pitting edema, unchanged since the last visit. He has been compliant with his furosemide regimen (120 mg daily) and dietary sodium restrictions, but he expresses frustration as the edema continues to limit his mobility and daily activities. He reports no new symptoms such as pain or redness in the affected areas.
In relation to his mental health, Mr. Fairfax continues to engage in cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) sessions. He reports that while his anxiety levels have slightly improved, he still grapples with occasional spikes, particularly surrounding his health issues. He is eager to explore additional coping strategies and techniques to manage these fluctuations more effectively.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + persistent dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + ongoing joint pain, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using six to seven times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 120 mg daily (unchanged). 7. Sertraline 100 mg daily.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 80, BP 128/75, RR 24, O2 sat 78% on room air
General: Elderly male in mild respiratory distress, appears fatigued but engaged. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.9, Hgb 10.5, Hct 31.5, Plt 210 2. BMP: Na 132, K 4.2, Cl 98, CO2 28, BUN 36, Cr 2.0, Glucose 92 3. BNP: 560 (slight increase). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.7 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax continues to experience significant respiratory symptoms. Given the persistent dyspnea and nocturnal wheezing, it is recommended to increase the frequency of his albuterol inhaler use and to consider a trial of a long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) to provide better control of his symptoms. A follow-up pulmonary function test is advised in one month to reassess lung function. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists despite the current furosemide dosage. Referral to nephrology is strongly recommended for further evaluation of renal function and potential adjustment of diuretic therapy. Reinforcement of dietary sodium restrictions continues to be essential. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax reports benefits from CBT. Continue sertraline 100 mg daily. Follow-up with psychiatry in one month for ongoing management and reassessment of treatment efficacy. Discuss potential adjunctive therapies, such as mindfulness techniques and relaxation exercises, to help manage anxiety.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
